Y_TB6r4jI9I.title: Why Some Ragusa Residents Had to Wait 30 Days to Go Home
Y_TB6r4jI9I.description:
In 1377, the trading city of Ragusa—now Dubrovnik—required people arriving from plague-affected places to wait 30 days before entering. Even residents returning home could be made to wait.

The city was trying to reduce the risk of plague without shutting down the trade it depended on. A later 40-day waiting period gave us the word quarantine.

UkwqGIqvink.title: Two Ancient Animals Found Together in a 250-Million-Year-Old Burrow
UkwqGIqvink.description:
Inside a fossilized burrow about 250 million years old, two very different animals were found together: Thrinaxodon, a small predator, and Broomistega, a young amphibian with injured ribs.

This short follows a possible explanation for how they came to share the shelter and were buried together. The fossil preserves their remains; the animals' final moments are a reconstruction.

fvRm9Vxwagk.title: The Taj Mahal Legend: Why the Architect Lost His Hands #TajMahal #Shorts
fvRm9Vxwagk.description:
One legend about the Taj Mahal tells of Ahmad, the architect placed in charge of its construction—and the terrible price he and his assistants paid after the monument was finished.

This short retells a story about skill, power and a ruler who feared that its creator might build something just as magnificent again. The tale is presented as a legend, not an established account of what happened to the builders.
